faq.title: Why would a client buy Beam instead of SAP / Oracle / ServiceNow / Workday AI?
faq.summary: Those products automate work inside their own object model.
faq.body: Those products automate work inside their own object model. Clients still have email, shared drives, legacy ERPs, SMS, country-specific portals, and exceptions the incumbent assistant cannot close. Beam is the intelligence layer that runs the process across systems, with a graph that must start and finish, evals on the steps that matter, and an audit log. The user stays in the screen they already live in. Beam writes back. Use this when the process spans two or more systems, is exception-heavy, or sits on a 15–30 year ERP the client will not rip out. Do not pick a fight inside a clean, single-module S/4 workflow the ERP already does well.

faq.title: How is this different from Anaplan / OneStream / other EPM?
faq.summary: EPM is a planning layer. Beam is not that database.
faq.body: EPM is a planning and data-model layer. If the client’s actual problem is "we have no planning model", that is an EPM deal. If the problem is "70 people in a room judging invoices because the ERP’s three-way match dies on exceptions", that is a Beam deal. They can coexist. Beam pulls what it needs, acts, and does not keep a second warehouse by default.

faq.title: You do not store the data. So how do you work?
faq.summary: We integrate, pull what is actionable, act, and discard the rest.
faq.body: We integrate through a custom integration builder and an out-of-the-box catalog. We pull, decide if it is actionable, act, and discard what we do not need. We are not a process-mining suite and not a data-lake vendor. If the client has no API and no export path, say so early.

faq.title: What makes a strong first workflow?
faq.summary: Start with repeatable, exception-heavy work that crosses systems and has a measurable outcome.
faq.body: A strong first workflow is frequent enough to matter, contains manual handoffs or re-keying, crosses two or more systems, and has exceptions that prevent simple rules-based automation. It also needs a named process owner, a usable API or export path, representative test data, and a baseline the client agrees to measure. Start with one narrow beachhead rather than an end-to-end transformation promise.

faq.title: When should we not pursue an opportunity?
faq.summary: Walk away when the problem is already solved by one module, cannot be accessed, or has no accountable owner.
faq.body: Do not force a Beam deal when a clean single-module ERP or EPM workflow already solves the problem well. Pause when there is no API or export path, no accountable process owner, no representative test data, or no measurable operational outcome. Also escalate expectations of unsupervised high-risk action. A vague innovation brief is not yet a qualified first workflow.

faq.title: Where does human approval sit?
faq.summary: Beam can prepare and recommend; accountable people retain high-risk approvals.
faq.body: Start read-first and recommend-first. The agent can gather evidence, prepare a decision, and propose an action while an accountable person approves high-risk steps such as payments, regulated decisions, or material client communications. The exact approval point is a workflow design decision. Put it into the audit trail and evaluate both the recommendation and the handoff.

faq.summary: Restricted. Do not state residency or on-prem as a generic promise.
faq.body: Do not state regional residency, on-prem, private-networking, or government readiness as a generic promise.
faq.restrictedReason: Regional deployment and sovereignty claims need commercial and security approval.
faq.requestBeamLabel: Request Beam for a deployment review.

faq.title: Every GM already bought a small AI tool. Why will this not be another one?
faq.summary: We pick one high-volume chain and put it into production with evals.
faq.body: We do not sprinkle assistants on unchanged processes. We pick one high-volume back-office chain, agree success criteria, put it into production with evals and exception paths, and only then expand. Local tool sprawl with zero upside is the default. The counter is a process-bank, a ranked first wave, and fees that can wait on proof.

faq.title: Why Beam instead of building this ourselves?
faq.summary: Partner owns the client and delivery center. Beam owns the factory.
faq.body: Priorities, not talent, are why in-house platform attempts stall. Beam’s job is the platform, the agent factory, and the production eval loop. The partner’s job is the client, the operating model, the humans in the delivery center, and the transformation story. We are not a rent-a-brand, and Beam is not staff-aug hiding in a partner logo.

faq.title: Do we expose the Beam brand?
faq.summary: Three legal shapes only.
faq.body: Partner-fronted / powered by Beam for brand-sensitive managed services. Joint when the client wants the technology vendor in the room. Beam-fronted, partner-introduced for a technical buyer. Do not invent a fourth shape on the call.

faq.title: What does the first engagement look like?
faq.summary: Qualify, diagnose, shadow, produce, then expand.
faq.body: Qualify the account and walk away when it is EPM or a single-module ERP assistant. Take an outside-in view and process interviews. Rank a first wave and agree success criteria. Shadow one process with test data. Produce with evals, exception paths, and an audit log. Expand along the value chain. License after value is visible.

faq.title: How do we define and measure success?
faq.summary: Agree the baseline, operational outcome, guardrails, and evaluation method before production.
faq.body: Define success for the named process before production. Capture the current baseline, select an operational outcome such as cycle time, throughput, exception resolution, or quality, document the human approval points, and agree how the workflow will be evaluated. Do not invent a universal ROI percentage. Beam and the partner should write the first success criteria together and use the result to decide whether to expand.

faq.summary: Flag early. Beam does not give legal advice.
faq.body: Use the checklist: named client, service line, whether Beam would be in the attest perimeter, who contracts, who hosts data, and whether white-label reduces conflict optics. Beam does not give legal advice. PwC risk must clear the motion.
faq.restrictedReason: Independence is a risk conversation, not a published legal answer.
faq.requestBeamLabel: Request Beam and loop partner risk. Do not treat this FAQ as legal advice.

faq.title: How do you keep accuracy from decaying?
faq.summary: Production feedback becomes clustered training data.
faq.body: Production feedback (thumbs, failed code nodes, low evals) becomes training data. Problems are clustered. One cluster is trained at a time, then regression-tested against the others.

playbooks.title: One-workflow shadow engagement
playbooks.summary: One client, one shared-services process, shadow environment, then a playbook.
playbooks.body:
Partner brings the named client, the process, and humans in the delivery center.
Beam brings the platform, an FDE, the agent graph, and evals.

Sequence:
1. Qualify the client and the process.
2. Run a 60-minute diagnostic.
3. Show a shadow workflow on test data.
4. Agree success criteria in writing.
5. File a Beam request for the shadow demo if it is not already scheduled.

Do not open Platform admin, Iris authoring, or a joint-venture workspace. Failure mode is request Beam.
